title: Diversity of plant and animal forms comes from different simple rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Diversity of plant and animal forms comes from different simple rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Most of the diversity and complexity in the forms of plants and animals arises because slightly different, essentially randomly picked simple growth rules lead to very different and often complex behavior.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is this basic phenomenon that I suspect is responsible for most of the diversity and complexity that we see in the forms of plants and animals.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Biological Pigmentation Patterns” (from p. 422), p. 422. Scope: forms of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-25: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.22

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Morphological diversity is documented, but the hypothesized rule-level causes and their randomness are not. The majority attribution cannot be inferred from pattern resemblance or simulations alone. Resolving it requires extensive new developmental perturbation and comparative data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map a representative sample of plant and animal morphologies to validated developmental rule sets, quantify rule and output distances, and estimate how much diversity and complexity is caused by small effectively random rule changes. The predicted pattern is large output divergence from small rule differences dominating other sources.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Environmental, selective, and historical causes are difficult to partition.

Developmental rules are unknown for most forms.

No natural probability distribution defines randomly picked growth rules.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.2

analysis feasibility: 0.22

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The computational phenomenon, that nearby simple rules diverge in form, is immediate to check. The biological claim that most diversity and complexity come from essentially random sampling of such rules is a historical cause that images and program catalogs do not record. Existing resources illustrate the mechanism and do not resolve its responsibility for most organismal form.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Show that small changes in simple growth rules change simulated form sharply, then ask whether real diversity is concentrated among traits whose genetic differences look like draws from a short random rule rather than like selected parameter tuning. A match between observed form diversity and the random-rule ensemble, without a selection signal, would support the claim; diversity that tracks measured functional optima would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Randomly picked is not observable from adult form.

Sensitivity of a model to its parameters does not show that evolution samples rules that way.

operationalizability: 0.35
